gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-psalter-pahlav: Crowded, retro, and loud about it. Styro packs its letters tight, while Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi lets its e gape wide and keeps capitals low, so the two trade pressure for breathing room.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Retro and tightly packed, Styro presses its sizable lowercase until the curves barely open, which gives it command. Punch goes to the heading; Noto Sans Rejang handles the quiet, open work.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-runic: Crowded letters with barely a gap in their curves give Styro its retro, commanding look over a sizable lowercase. Styro shouts; Noto Sans Runic, big x-height and open curves, speaks plainly.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Retro punch, then daylight. Styro crowds its letters for a commanding start, and Noto Sans Samaritan, hefty with open curves, keeps line after line comfortable and quick to move through.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-saurashtra: Styro presses its lowercase so tight that the letters feel crowded and the curves barely open. Styro brings the command; Noto Sans Saurashtra brings counters open to the outside.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-sc: Styro packs its retro, commanding lowercase so tightly that every curve nearly closes on itself, which is hard to miss. Noto Sans SC leaves its curves open; that gap is the point.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Styro crowds its sizable lowercase into a tight, retro block with barely any gap in the curves. And Styro earns its keep when big and brief, beside the open, bulky forms of Noto Sans Sharada.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Styro brings retro command, its lowercase pressed tight enough to feel crowded. And Noto Sans Siddham, with its large central band and wide-hanging s, makes paragraphs read in a friendly, open way.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Noto Sans Sinhala lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase. Give it a modest size so its far-apart curve endings stay visible, since crowded, retro Styro already supplies the punch above.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Retro through and through, Styro crowds its sizable lowercase until the curves barely open. But Noto Sans Soyombo, with a generous x-height and wide, unclosed mouths, gives the screen room to breathe.
